metadata.name: Ecodesign for Angular
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Angular: OnPush change detection, lazy routes, subscriptions torn down.

detection.name: Angular — change detection
detection.description: Default change detection re-checks every binding on every event (RGESN Frontend).

rules.title: Component without OnPush
rules.description: With the default strategy Angular re-evaluates every binding of every component after any event, anywhere. On a large page that is thousands of checks for one keystroke.
rules.recommendation: Set changeDetection: ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush and drive updates through immutable inputs or signals. Verify the check frequency with the profiler.
rules.note: A single OnPush or signal anywhere in the file silences the rule, so a file holding several components needs each one checked. Default detection is a reasonable choice on a small, rarely updated component.
rules.source_note: Adapted from the Green Codex rule LANG-ANGULAR-001 (Institut du Numerique Responsable), whose rule content is published under CC BY 4.0. Reworded for this format; the patterns are specific to this audit.

rules.title: Method called from a template
rules.description: A method in a binding runs on every change-detection pass, which is far more often than its result changes. The cost is invisible in the template and real on the device.
rules.recommendation: Precompute the value in the component, or expose it as a pipe with pure: true so the result is cached.
rules.source_note: Adapted from the Green Codex rule LANG-ANGULAR-003 (Institut du Numerique Responsable), whose rule content is published under CC BY 4.0. Reworded for this format; the patterns are specific to this audit.

rules.title: Subscription never torn down
rules.description: A subscription that outlives its component keeps the component, its template and everything they capture alive. Navigating back and forth then leaks one copy per visit.
rules.recommendation: Prefer the async pipe, which unsubscribes for you. Otherwise take until a destroy subject and complete it in ngOnDestroy.
rules.note: One takeUntil, one async pipe or one unsubscribe anywhere in the file silences the rule. Where several subscriptions coexist, check that each has its own teardown.
rules.source_note: Adapted from the Green Codex rule LANG-ANGULAR-003 (Institut du Numerique Responsable), whose rule content is published under CC BY 4.0. Reworded for this format; the patterns are specific to this audit.
